title: Decision Junction — Single Next Action
prompt:
Edit the first referenced Nudge mobile workout UI to correct the decision hierarchy while preserving the airport-wayfinding visual system from both references. Create one polished high-fidelity portrait phone screen at 9:16.

The product principle is: Nudge carries the planning burden. The screen must communicate exactly three layers in order: 1) here is what is happening, 2) here is the single next action to take, 3) here are the other exercises the user can jump to instead. There must be no extra recommendation, no second suggested path, and no duplicate presentation of alternative choices.

Keep: white Nudge header; black route band PLAN / PERFORMANCE / COOLDOWN / REVIEW with PERFORMANCE highlighted in airport yellow; current exercise context “02 SHOULDER PRESS”, “Set 2 of 3”, weight 35 lb and reps 10; and the exceptionally large airport-yellow “START SET” action panel with a bold black right arrow. The START SET panel is Nudge’s one clear directed next action and must remain the dominant interactive element, easy to hit while grabbing weights and getting into position.

Remove the entire “NEXT UP / Shoulder press is ready / GO NEXT / STAY HERE” section. Do not replace it with another recommendation card or choice.

Clarify concurrent status without creating a decision: directly below the current exercise and START SET area, use one compact black information band reading “01 GOBLET SQUAT · RESTING” with a visible timer “1:12”. This is passive context only, not a control and not an instruction to switch.

Below that, show the quiet manual escape hatch titled “YOUR ROUTE · 2 OF 4”. Show three compact full-width tappable rows: “01 GOBLET SQUAT · 3/3 SETS” marked RESTING, “03 ONE-ARM ROW · 0/3 SETS” marked READY, and “04 DEAD BUG · 0/2 SETS” marked READY. Use bold two-digit identifiers, plain status text, large tap targets, and restrained chevrons. Make this section clearly selectable but visually subordinate to START SET: white or pale concrete rows, thin graphite rules, black type, tiny yellow status accents. The route list is the only way alternatives are presented.

Remove the stray Catalog header label. Do not use Change exercise, Next up, Go next, Stay here, dropdowns, modals, floating actions, trophies, flags, streaks, celebration, urgency, gradients, shadows, rounded cards, or decorative illustration. Use saturated airport yellow, jet black, signal white, pale concrete, graphite, humanist transport-signage typography, strict rectangular geometry, generous spacing, oversized identifiers, and bold arrows. Ensure all text is legible and the hierarchy reads instantly: context, one next action, optional route.
